significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that backtracking is caused by an ordered two-stage mechanism in which "an error/inconsistency detector writes a signal" and then "suppresses the current reasoning path and up-weights alternative continuations," with this circuit strengthening through RL; this is a form-(ii) causal decomposition that fixes the order of two computations rather than merely showing a decodable feature. It establishes both a phenomenon—RL changes useful and reflexive backtracking—and a mechanism that predicts detector activity before rerouting, increased circuit strength after RL, induced correction under stimulation, and reduced looping under suppression; this would sharpen the behavioral account of reevaluation described in the DeepSeek-R1 technical report (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025). Verified false would rule out the unified detect-then-reroute and RL-emergence explanation, although it would not select a specific alternative, and the true and false branches are distinguishable despite the somewhat loose phrase "largely absent." In the topic-substitution check, generic efficient-reasoning interpretability would not supply the ordered detector/rerouter decomposition or its opposite causal effects on correction and looping, so the score remains above the topic median.

reach.justification: The transferable handles named by the claim are the "detector-direction," causal stimulation or suppression of that signal, and "detector-gated correction" as an inference-time control. This is an online ex-ante handle: after inconsistency is detected but before the model completes the erroneous or wastefully looping trajectory, it can invoke correction or suppress further backtracking, giving inference-system designers an action window rather than merely explaining a completed failure. Re-extraction on another model would still predict the detect-before-reroute ordering and stronger signal in RL-trained than base checkpoints, but it does not specify a quantitative threshold or scaling law, and its asserted scope is RL-trained reasoners rather than multiple architectures, modalities, or non-AI settings. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score because the topic alone supplies neither the detector-gated control nor its two-sided correction/looping use; downstream uptake could include researchers and practitioners building or serving reasoning models.
